transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess what brings me in is that I’ve been having a hard time shaking this feeling that people around me are sort of… watching what I’m doing. Not everyone, but certain people in the arts scene and finance circles here in Cincinnati.

I work with clients, and I keep noticing things — like who gets invited to what, the topics on panels, where people sit near me at events — and it feels like they’re sending these little signals about which clients I’ve met with or what I’m involved in. And I know, I know, Cincinnati can be a small town socially, especially if you go to enough fundraisers and gallery things, you start seeing the same faces everywhere. But even when I tell myself it might just be coincidence, I can’t really let it go. It’s been bothering me enough that I figured I should talk to someone.
When you say people are sending signals about your clients or your activities, do you feel like they’re trying to communicate something specific to you, or maybe even influence your actions?

Yeah, I think… I mean, I don’t know if they’re trying to tell me one exact sentence or anything, but it feels like they’re making it clear they know who I’m meeting with. Like an invitation will come through, or a panel topic will be weirdly close to something I talked about with a client, or someone will sit near me at an event who has no real reason to be there.

And Cincinnati is like that, you know — the arts people and finance people overlap more than you’d think, especially at those fundraiser things with the same wine and the same sponsors every time. But it feels too coordinated sometimes. Like they’re tracking my client meetings and sort of nudging me, or letting me know they’re aware. I try to tell myself it could just be coincidence, but I can’t really shake it.
Do you ever feel like everyday things people say or do — like something in a conversation, a TV show, or even a song — are directed at you personally or meant just for you to understand?

Yeah… kind of. Not so much TV or songs, I don’t really pay attention to those in that way, but with conversations and events, yes. Like an invitation will show up, or a panel topic will be just a little too close to something I discussed with a client, and I start thinking, okay, that’s not random.

And then at these Cincinnati arts fundraisers — which, honestly, they’re all the same after a while, same sponsors, same people pretending the cheese plate is good — someone will sit near me who I know is connected to finance or to a client somehow. It feels like it’s meant for me to notice. Like they’re not saying it directly, but they’re signaling that they know who I’ve been meeting with.

I do try to talk myself down and say it could be coincidence, because Cincinnati can be weirdly small socially, but I can’t really let it go once I notice it.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts aren't entirely your own, or like someone is putting thoughts into your mind?

Um… I don’t think so? Not like someone is putting thoughts in there, no. My thoughts feel like mine, even when they’re kind of racing around or I’m replaying things too much.

I mean, sometimes after meetings I’ll go over conversations in my head way too long — like, did I say the right thing, did that person mean something by that comment — but that’s more me getting stuck on it, I think. Not like an outside voice or someone planting an idea. At least, I haven’t noticed it that way.
Have you ever felt that certain events, objects, or people’s actions have a special or hidden meaning that’s directed specifically at you, even if others wouldn’t see it that way?

Yeah, that’s… that’s pretty much what I mean. Like I know if someone else looked at it they might say, “Oh, that’s just Cincinnati being small,” and maybe it is, but it doesn’t feel that way to me.

It’s more like certain things line up too neatly — an invitation shows up after I’ve met with someone, or a panel topic sounds weirdly close to something I just discussed with a client, or a person from one of those arts-and-finance circles ends up sitting right near me. And those events, they’re all kind of connected anyway, you know, same donors, same bank logos on the program, same people acting like they just happened to run into each other.

So yeah, I do feel like there’s a hidden meaning in it sometimes. Like it’s directed at me, like they’re quietly letting me know they know who I’m meeting with. I try to tell myself other people wouldn’t see it, or that I’m overreading it, but once I notice it, I can’t really just drop it.
Have you ever felt that something you did, like a gesture or action, was meant to communicate something directly to you, even if no one else would understand that connection?

Yeah, I think so… though it’s not always like one gesture exactly. It’s more the placement of things, or what people do around me.

Like if I go to one of those arts events in Cincinnati and someone from a bank or a foundation ends up sitting close by right after I’ve had a client meeting that week, it feels like that’s not just seating. It feels like it’s meant to communicate, like, we know who you’ve been talking to. And then maybe there’s an invitation or some panel topic that sounds too close to a conversation I had, and I start connecting it.

I know that probably sounds like I’m making too much of it. I do tell myself maybe it’s coincidence, or just the same small circle of people. But it gets stuck in my head, and I can’t really shake the feeling that certain people are sending these little signals specifically for me to notice.
Have you ever felt that your actions or behaviors were being controlled by some outside force or that someone was trying to influence what you do without you being able to stop it?

I don’t know if I’d say controlled, exactly. I still go where I decide to go, I still meet with my clients, do my work, all that. But… it does feel like people are trying to influence me, or make me aware of something.

Like, I came in because this has been going on for a while — I keep feeling like certain people in the arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati are quietly tracking who I’m meeting with. And then I’ll see these little things, like an invitation that shows up, or a panel topic that sounds a little too close to something I just talked about, or someone sitting near me at an event, and it feels like a signal.

So not like they’re moving my hands or making me do things. More like they’re trying to steer me, or get in my head a little, and even when I tell myself it could be coincidence, I can’t really drop it.

Do you ever feel like things that are not directly related to you — like strangers’ conversations, the placement of objects, or events in the world — are actually about you or meant for you to understand specifically?

Yeah… yes, that’s probably the main reason I came in, honestly.

It’s like, I’ll be at some Cincinnati arts thing — and I don’t even go to all of them, just the ones where clients or people I know might be — and then suddenly someone from one of the banks or a foundation is sitting near me, or an invitation comes through that lines up too closely with who I just met with. Or a panel topic will be about something that sounds almost exactly like a conversation I had with a client, and I know panels get planned in advance, I know that, but still.

And then I start thinking it’s meant for me to understand. Like they’re quietly showing me they know which clients I’m meeting with. I keep trying to tell myself Cincinnati is small, the arts and finance people overlap, everyone knows everyone, but I can’t really let it go once I notice it. It feels too specific.
Have you ever felt that something you experienced — like a sensation, a thought, or something you saw — was deliberately placed there by someone to send you a message that only you would understand?

Yeah… I mean, that’s sort of what it feels like. Not like a voice or anything, more like… I’ll see an invitation come in, or there’s a panel topic at one of these arts events, and it lines up too closely with something I just talked about with a client.

And I know, I know Cincinnati has these overlapping circles — finance people, arts boards, foundations, all that. I’ve been around that enough to know people talk. I also don’t want to sound like I think every little thing is about me. But for a while now I’ve been pretty convinced certain people are tracking who I meet with and then putting these little signs in front of me. Like who sits near me at an event, or what the event is about, or an invite showing up at just the right time.

It feels deliberately placed, like it’s meant for me to understand: “we know.” And even when I try to tell myself it could be coincidence, I can’t really drop it.
